title: Curse of Viradha
introduction: Rama and Lakshmana come to know about the curse of Viradha. Viradha desires to die in then hands of Rama according to the amendment given by the cursing authority, and thus he will be killed and relieved of his curse by Rama, and his elimination of negative forces starts with the elimination of Viradha. At the time of release from his curse, Viradha advises Rama to go to Sage Sharabhanga, who can advise Rama properly. It is said whenever a superior being is approached, he shall not be neared empty-handedly. So, the elimination of Viradha, first act of Rama to safeguard the diinajana parirakshana in Dandaka forests is the gift that Rama takes to the Sage Sharabhanga in next chapter. This is not a separate chapter in Baroda edition. But in Gorakhpur and Eastern versions it is a separate one.
closing: The episode of Viraadha assumes some importance in Hindu mythology. It may be observed that Viraadha drops down Seetha, lifts and carries Rama and Lakshmana far away from Seetha, where Rama and Lakshmana kill Viraadha. aadhyaatma raamaayana which occurs in the chapter 61 of brahmaanmda puraana also narrates this episode of Viradha as a one to one fight, herein Rama affronts and kills him straight. But in Valmiki Ramayana, Viradha takes away Seetha first and then Rama and Lakshmana, too. A question arises as to why the demon should snatch Seetha away and later carry Rama and Lakshmana to a distant place from Seetha. It is part of the scheme that Rama kills no demon or sinner in the presence of Seetha, including Ravana, for she is that benevolent one to all the sinners and pardons them if surrendered in faith at her feet, as an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi. Our concern here is with skaanda purana , a Shiva Puraana, in which Viradha's episode is explained detailedly. The skaanda puraana puts it as:

On seeing Seetha Viraaadha thought, " She is the Supreme goddess through whom heavens can be obtained by salvation and also release from the bondage [of demon's body ] On just seeing Her, relieved is this body cage, so with all my devotion, I steal Her ." etc. Hence vi raadha meant to be verily, devout, like Radha of Krishna. When chased and hurt by Rama and Lakshmana, the demon releases Seetha, but carries both the brothers away. For this distancing Rama and Lakshmana from Seetha, it is said that Rama does not kill any demon in the presence of Seetha, for she graciously condones the mischief of the demons, if they are true devotees.
Again in skaanda puraana, at the end of this Viraaadha episode, the phala shruti [Fruit of Listening] it is narrated as:
" Those that always listen or let listen this episode of virAdha, all their sins are absolved, undoubtedly .. skaanda pauraana
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 4th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana,the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ह्रियमाणौ तु काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा सीता रघूत्तमौ |
उच्चैः स्वरेण चुक्रोश प्रगृह्य सु महाभुजौ
verses.iast:
hriyamāṇau tu kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā sītā raghūttamau |
uccaiḥ svareṇa cukrośa pragṛhya su mahābhujau
verses.translation: On seeing those two very dexterous scions of Kakutstha, and the best ones from Raghu dynasty, namely Rama and Lakshmana, grabbed and being carried off, Seetha screamed in a high-pitched voice.

glosses.meaning: being carried off, very great, shouldered ones [very dexterous ones]
scions of Kakutstha, the best ones from Raghu dynasty Rama and Lakshmana

verses.devanagari:
एष दाशरथी रामः सत्यवान् शीलवान् शुचिः |
रक्षसा रौद्र रूपेण ह्रियते सह लक्ष्मणः

rakśasā raudra rūpeṇa hriyate saha lakśmaṇaḥ

glosses.meaning: truth abiding one, virtuous one, flawless one
by demon ,with ferocious look, being carried off.

verses.devanagari:

माम् हरः उत्सृज्य काकुत्स्थौ नमस्ते राक्षसोत्तमः
verses.iast:

mām haraḥ utsṛjya kākutsthau namaste rākśasottamaḥ

glosses.itrans: maam R^ikaa tathaa shaarduula dviipinaH bhaksha iSyanti
glosses.iast: mām ṛkā tathā śārdūla dvīpinaḥ bhakśa iṣyanti
glosses.devanagari: मां ऋका तथा शार्दूल द्वीपिनः भक्श इष्यन्ति
glosses.meaning: me, wild-bears, like that, tigers, panthers, to eat, they aspire

verses.devanagari:
तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा वैदेह्याः राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वेगम् प्रचक्रतुर् वीरौ वधे तस्य दुरात्मनः

tasyāḥ tat vacanam śrutvā vaidehyāḥ rāma lakśmaṇau |
vegam pracakratur vīrau vadhe tasya durātmanaḥ

glosses.meaning: her, Vaidehi's, that, utterance, on hearing

verses.devanagari:
तस्य रौद्रस्य सौमित्रिः सव्यम् बाहुम् बभञ्ज ह |

verses.translation: Soumitri indeed severed the left arm of that ferocious one, while Rama rent the right arm of that demon with his might.

glosses.itrans: tasya raudrasya savyam baahum babhanja ha
glosses.iast: tasya raudrasya savyam bāhum babhanja ha

verses.devanagari:

धरण्याम् मेघ संकाशो वज्र भिन्न इव अचलः

verses.devanagari:

उद्यंयोद्यंय च अपि एनम् स्थण्डिले निष्पिपेषतुः

glosses.meaning: with fists, with hands, with feet

verses.devanagari:

glosses.meaning: by two swords, even, sheared off

verses.devanagari:
तम् प्रेक्ष्य रामः सुभृशम् अवध्यम् अचल उपमम् |
भयेषु अभय दः श्रीमान् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:

verses.translation: On observing that the mountain-similar demon is ineradicable that easily, then Rama, the sublime one, and the bestower of shelter in fear, spoke this sentence to Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:

शस्त्रेण युधि निर्जेतुम् राक्षसम् निखनावहे
verses.iast:
tapasā puruṣavyāghra rākśaso'yam na śakyate |
śastreṇa yudhi nirjetum rākśasam nikhanāvahe
verses.translation: "Oh! Manly-tiger Lakshmana, it is impossible to overpower this demon with weapons in a confrontation, hence, let's bury this demon...

glosses.meaning: in war, by weapons, to overpower

verses.devanagari:
कुंजर्स्य इव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्य अस्य लक्ष्मण! |
वने अस्मिन् सुमहद् श्वभ्रम् खन्यताम् रौद्रवर्चसः

glosses.meaning: for furious one, for ferocious, reprobate, for this, demon

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा लक्ष्मणम् रामः प्रदरः खन्यताम् इति |
तस्थौ विराधम् आक्र्ंय कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्
verses.iast:
iti uk{}tvā lakśmaṇam rāmaḥ pradaraḥ khanyatām iti |
tasthau virādham ākrṃya kaṇṭhe pādena vīryavān
verses.translation: On saying to Lakshmana that a trench shall be dug...' then Rama repressively placed his foot on the throat of Viradha, and stood by.

glosses.meaning: Viradha is, with foot, on the throat, overcoming [repressing,] stood in readiness.

verses.devanagari:
तत् श्रुत्वा राघवेण उक्तम् राक्षसः प्रश्रितम् वचः |

verses.iast:

idam provāca kākutstham virādhaḥ puruṣarṣabham
verses.translation: On hearing that said by Raghava, demon Viradha sincerely spoke these humble words to Rama, the finest one from Kakutstha dynasty.

glosses.meaning: that, on hearing, what by Raghava, said

verses.devanagari:
हतोऽहम् पुरुषव्याघ्रः शक्र तुल्य बलेन वै |

verses.iast:
hato'ham puruṣavyāghraḥ śakra tulya balena vai |
mayā tu pūrvam tvam mohān na jñātaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: "Dead I am, oh! Manly-tiger and a coequal of Indra in your strength... I have fallaciously not identified you earlier... oh, best one among men...

verses.devanagari:
कौसल्या सुप्रजातः तात रामः त्वम् विदितो मया |
वैदेही च महाभागा लक्ष्मणः च महायशाः
verses.iast:

verses.translation: "Oh, sire, now I have known you to be Rama, the son of Kausalya... and even propitious Seetha and greatly renowned one Lakshmana are now known to me...

glosses.meaning: Lakshmana, too, great, renowned one [are now known.]

verses.devanagari:
अभि शापाद् अहम् घोरम् प्रविष्टो राक्ष्सीम् तनुम् |
तुंबुरुः नाम गन्धर्वः शप्तो वैश्रवणेन हि
verses.iast:
abhi śāpād aham ghoram praviṣṭo rākśsīm tanum |
tumburuḥ nāma gandharvaḥ śapto vaiśravaṇena hi
verses.translation: "By curse I had to enter this ghoulish demon's body, but I am a celestial gandharva, named Tumburu and Kubera cursed me...

verses.devanagari:
प्रसाद्यमानः च मया सोऽब्रवीत् माम् महायशाः |
यदा दाशरथी रमः त्वाम् वधिष्यति संयुगे
तदा प्रकृतिम् आपन्नो भवान् स्वर्गम् गमिष्यति |
verses.iast:
prasādyamānaḥ ca mayā so'bravīt mām mahāyaśāḥ |
yadā dāśarathī ramaḥ tvām vadhiṣyati saṃyuge
tadā prakṛtim āpanno bhavān svargam gamiṣyati |
verses.translation: "When entreated by me, he that greatly renowned Kubera said to me, 'When Dasharatha's Rama kills you in a fight... then you will attain your nature of celestial body and you will go to heavens...'

glosses.meaning: entreated, he was, also, by me
then, natural state [celestial body,] you attain

verses.devanagari:
अनुपस्थीयमानो माम् स क्रुद्धो व्याजहार ह
इति वैश्रवणो राजा रंभ आसक्तम् उवाच ह |
verses.iast:
anupasthīyamāno mām sa kruddho vyājahāra ha
iti vaiśravaṇo rājā rambha āsak{}tam uvāca ha |
verses.translation: " King Kubera thus cursed angrily me for not presenting myself in his service when I was interested in a celestial dancer Rambha, and indeed he alone said this curse-clearance to me...

verses.devanagari:
तव प्रसादान् मुक्तो अहम् अभिशापात् सु दारुणात्
भुवनम् स्वम् गमिष्यामि स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु परंतप |
verses.iast:
tava prasādān muk{}to aham abhiśāpāt su dāruṇāt
bhuvanam svam gamiṣyāmi svasti vo'stu parantapa |
verses.translation: " And by your grace I am released from this utterly hideous cruse, and now I wish to go to my own heavenly abode, oh, firestorm of enemies, let safety betide you all...
notes: The celestial beings are called sura and their antagonists are a-sura . There are many sura beings living in heavens and netherworlds. To name a few, they are uraga, garuda, gandharva, kimpuruśa, siddha, sādhya, vidyādhara, cāraṇa, apsara, yakśa, guhyaka, bhūta, khecara and the like. Of them gandharva-s are amiable beings for their expertise in performing arts. The apsara beings are the divine courtesans and among them are four apsara beings of high order. They are Rambha, Urvashi, Menaka and Tilottama . These four are instrumental to Indra, to incite and allure sages from their austere penance, lest they may win over the ship on heavens from Indra. The present gandharva, namely Tumburu, in his courting with Rambha had belated his services to Kubera, the Chief Divinity for Wealth Management. Hence Kubera cursed this gandharva to become the demon called Viradha, but yet this Tumburu alias Viradha is the devotee of Goddess Lakshmi. The antagonists of sura are a-sura beings and all sorts of demons, monsters, etc., come under this category and they are not devils or Satan's stooges, but they equal the capabilities of sura beings. Prof. Ranade observes that "Dr. R.G. Bhandarkar, in an important article in the B.Br.A.S. Journal makes the following interesting suggestion. The Sanskrit equivalent of the word demon viz., 'Asurya' may here refer to the 'Assyrian' country. 'Assyrian and 'Asuryan' being philologically identical, the 'y' and the 'u' being interchangeable as in Greek..."

glosses.meaning: to heavens, mine, [now,] to go, I wish

verses.devanagari:
इतो वसति धर्मात्मा शरभङ्गः प्रतापवान्
अध्यर्थ योजने तातः महर्षिः सूर्य संनिभः |

ito vasati dharmātmā śarabhañgaḥ pratāpavān
adhyartha yojane tātaḥ maharṣiḥ sūrya saṃnibhaḥ |
tam kśipram abhigaccha tvam sa te śreyo abhidhāsyati
verses.translation: "Oh, Sire, att one and half yojana-s of distance from here Sage Sharabhanga, a great saint of virtue, and an efficacious sage with sun-like resplendence dwells, you shall quickly approach him for he advises you opportunely... [3-4-20-21]

glosses.meaning: from here, after one and half, yojana-s
virtuous one, efficacious one, with sun-like resplendence

verses.devanagari:
अवटे च अपि माम् राम निक्षिप्य कुशली व्रज |
रक्षसाम् गत सत्त्वानाम् एष धर्मः सनातनः
अवटे ये निधीयन्ते तेषाम् लोकाः सनातनाः |
verses.iast:
avaṭe ca api mām rāma nikśipya kuśalī vraja |
rakśasām gata sattvānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
avaṭe ye nidhīyante teṣām lokāḥ sanātanāḥ |
verses.translation: "Rama you go safely on burying me in a pit... this is the age-old custom for those demons that lost vitality... those that are inhumed in pit, to them there will be the worlds of manes..."

glosses.meaning: in a pit, also, thus, me

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थम् विराधः शर पीडितः
बभूव स्वर्ग संप्राप्तो न्यस्त देहो महाबलः |
verses.iast:
evam uk{}tvā tu kākutstham virādhaḥ śara pīḍitaḥ
babhūva svarga samprāpto nyasta deho mahābalaḥ |
verses.translation: "And on saying thus to Rama that Viradha who is hurt by arrows became heaven-worthy on leaving his body.

glosses.meaning: on leaving, body, of mighty, strength.

verses.devanagari:
तत् श्रुत्वा राघवः वाक्यम् लक्ष्मणम् व्यादिदेश ह
कुंजर्स्य इव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्य अस्य लक्ष्मण! |
वने अस्मिन् सुमहत् श्वभ्रम् खन्यताम् रौद्रकर्मणः
इति उक्त्वा लक्ष्मणम् रामः प्रदरः खन्यताम् इति |
तस्थौ विराधम् आक्रंय कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्
verses.iast:
tat śrutvā rāghavaḥ vākyam lakśmaṇam vyādideśa ha
kuñjarsya iva raudrasya rākśasasya asya lakśmaṇa! |
vane asmin sumahat śvabhram khanyatām raudrakarmaṇaḥ
iti uk{}tvā lakśmaṇam rāmaḥ pradaraḥ khanyatām iti |
tasthau virādham ākraṃya kaṇṭhe pādena vīryavān
verses.translation: And Raghava on hearing those words of the demon ordered Lakshmana, "Lakshmana, a very deep pit be dug for this furious and ferocious reprobate in this forest, as though for an elephant..." On saying to Lakshmana that a trench shall be dug...' then Rama repressively placed his foot on the throat of Viradha, and stood by.

glosses.meaning: for furious one, for ferocious, reprobate, for this, demon
very, deep, pit, be dug. viiryavaan = valiant one Rama [spoke thus to Lakshmana]
Viradha is, with foot, on the throat, overcoming [repressing,] stood in readiness.

verses.devanagari:

अखनत् पार्श्वतः तस्य विराधस्य महात्मनः
verses.iast:
tataḥ khanitram ādāya lakśmaṇaḥ śvabhram uttamam |

verses.translation: Then, on taking a digging tool Lakshmana dug a deep pit beside the great soul Viradha.

glosses.meaning: beside of, that, of Viradha, the great soul.

verses.devanagari:

विराधम् प्राक्षिपत् श्वभ्रे नदन्तम् भैरव स्वनम्
verses.iast:

verses.translation: On releasing his throat from the stamping of Rama, he that long eared, lurid voiced Viradha is ensconced in that pit while he is still blaring with his horrific voice.

verses.devanagari:
तम् आहवे दारुणम् आशु विक्रमौ
स्थिरौ उभौ संयति राम लक्ष्मणौ |
मुदान्वितौ चिक्षिपतुर् भयावहम्
नदन्तम् उत्क्षिप्य बिलेन राक्ष्सम्
verses.iast:
tam āhave dāruṇam āśu vikramau
sthirau ubhau saṃyati rāma lakśmaṇau |
mudānvitau cikśipatur bhayāvaham
nadantam utkśipya bilena rākśsam
verses.translation: Those deftly victorious ones Rama and Lakshmana who compose themselves in a given fight, both have gladly raised that Viradha, a ghoulish one in fight, a terrifying demon who is still blaring, with all their might and hurled him into the pit.

glosses.meaning: in a fight, who compose themselves

verses.devanagari:
अवध्यताम् प्रेक्ष्य महासुरस्य तौ
शितेन शस्त्रेण तदा नरर्षभौ |
समर्थ्य च अत्यर्थ विशारदौ उभौ
बिले विरधस्य वधम् प्रचक्रतुः
verses.iast:
avadhyatām prekśya mahāsurasya tau
śitena śastreṇa tadā nararṣabhau |
samarthya ca atyartha viśāradau ubhau
bile viradhasya vadham pracakratuḥ
verses.translation: On observing the indestructibility of that demon with any weapon, however sharp it might be, those two best ones among men that are very expertly skilled have thought over well and undertook the elimination of that great demon in a pit.

glosses.meaning: very, in skills, experts [very expertly skilled]
of great, demon, of that, Viradha's
in pit, elimination, they have undertaken.

verses.devanagari:
स्वयम् विराधेन हि मृत्युम् आत्मनः
प्रसह्य रामेण वधार्थम् ईप्सितः |
निवेदितः कानन चारिणा स्वयम्
न मे वधः शस्त्र कृतो भवेत् इति
verses.iast:
svayam virādhena hi mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
prasahya rāmeṇa vadhārtham īpsitaḥ |
niveditaḥ kānana cāriṇā svayam
na me vadhaḥ śastra kṛto bhavet iti
verses.translation: Viradha himself preferred his death at the hands of Rama and desired for a long to be killed by Rama and that forest walker himself appraised that, "Killing me with any weapon is impossible..."

glosses.meaning: by Viradha, on his own, of his own death

glosses.itrans: me shastra kR^itaH vadhaH na bhavet iti
glosses.iast: me śastra kṛtaḥ vadhaḥ na bhavet iti
glosses.devanagari: मे शस्त्र कृतः वधः न भवेत् इति
glosses.meaning: to me, weapon, oriented, killing, not, possible, thus as

verses.devanagari:
तदेव रामेण निशंय भाषितम्
कृता मतिः तस्य बिल प्रवेशने |
बिलम् च तेन अति बलेन रक्षसा
प्रवेश्यमानेन वनम् विनादितम्
verses.iast:
tadeva rāmeṇa niśaṃya bhāṣitam
kṛtā matiḥ tasya bila praveśane |
bilam ca tena ati balena rakśasā
praveśyamānena vanam vināditam
verses.translation: On listening to that which is said by Viradha, Rama resolved his mind to cast him into pit, and when that mighty demon is being flung into the pit the whole forest blared with that demon's cries.

glosses.meaning: that, said [by Viradha,] only, on listening

glosses.itrans: raameNa tasya bila praveshane kR^ita matiH
glosses.iast: rāmeṇa tasya bila praveśane kṛta matiḥ
glosses.devanagari: रामेण तस्य बिल प्रवेशने कृत मतिः
glosses.meaning: by Rama, his, into pit, entering [casting him,] resolved, in mind
into pit, while being entered [while flungh in to pit]

glosses.itrans: ati balena tena raakshasaa vanam vinaaditam
glosses.iast: ati balena tena rākśasā vanam vināditam
glosses.devanagari: अति बलेन तेन राक्शसा वनं विनादितं
glosses.meaning: very, mighty one, by him, that demon, forest, is verily, blared.

verses.devanagari:
प्रहृष्ट रूपौ इव राम लक्ष्मणौ
विराधम् उर्व्याम् प्रदरे निपात्य तम् |
ननन्दतुः वीत भयौ महावने
शिलाभिः अन्तर् दधतुः च राक्षसम्
verses.iast:
prahṛṣṭa rūpau iva rāma lakśmaṇau
virādham urvyām pradare nipātya tam |
nanandatuḥ vīta bhayau mahāvane
śilābhiḥ antar dadhatuḥ ca rākśasam
verses.translation: Rama and Lakshmana felt happy by way of their look in burying Viradha in the pit of the earth, and on burying him they two felt rejoiced for gone is the fear in that great forest, and within the pit they have also concealed him with boulders in order to make it a burial-chamber to the departed soul.
notes: Everywhere Rama patiently performs these funeral rites, whether it is demon, eagle or a monkey, if dead in his presence. Here also, Viradha's grave is covered with stones and boulders, as a kind of Stonehenge.

glosses.meaning: demon is, with boulders, within, concealed, also.

verses.devanagari:
ततः तु तौ कांचन चित्र कार्मुकौ
निहत्य रक्षः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम् |
विजह्रतुः तौ मुदितौ महावने
दिवि स्थितौ चन्द्र दिवाकरौ इव
verses.iast:
tataḥ tu tau kāñcana citra kārmukau
nihatya rakśaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm |
vijahratuḥ tau muditau mahāvane
divi sthitau candra divākarau iva
verses.translation: Then they two who have dazzling golden bows have eliminated that demon and retrieved Seetha, and they gladly journeyed on in that great forest like the two entities abiding on the skies, namely the Sun and Moon.
notes: The simile of sun and moon is of some importance. It will not be clear as to, who is compared with Sun and who with Moon, unless some ancient commentaries are touched. Rama is compared with Chandra, the Moon, because, Moon will not travel without his wives. All the celestial stars are the wives of the Moon, and they twinkle before the Moon's arrival, in order to welcome him into the night. Hence Rama is suffixed with Chandra, compounding to Sri Ramachandra. On the other hand, Sun does not travel along with his wife, namely Chaya, the Shadow, but she always will be at his hind. We the living beings are in between the Sun and his wife Chaya. If we face Sun in the morning times, she will be at our back, and in the evenings, when the Sun is at our back, Chaya, shadow will be in front of us, reminding us of our lengthening shadow of life. Thus we are in between the light and shadow. The Sun is also called karma saakshi, [Witness of Deeds.] Our own shadow, shortens with the ascending Sun and lengthens as the dusk of our day or life increases. Hence Sun's travel is wife-less one, and Lakshmana is thus compared with the Sun, for he does not have his wife travelling with him now. And Lakshmana is another karma saakshi [Witness of Events] in the Ramayana. In another way of commenting it is said that both of them are said to be moon-like in their appeasing personalities and sun-like in their radiant valour.
